# The exact active-compatibility dual for three triangle fibers

Continue with positive planar triangles at indices0,1,2, but allow
(K0+K2)/2 to touch K1. This note derives the extra dual terms exactly. It does
not reuse the strict-containment midpoint lemma after its hypotheses fail.

## 1. Three support constraints, with all contact ties retained

Write the middle triangle as

    K1={x:n_l.x<=h_l, l=1,2,3},

with outward unit normals n_l. Compatibility is equivalent to the three
inequalities

    2h_l-h_K0(n_l)-h_K2(n_l)>=0.                                  (1)

Allow independent affine maps x -> A_z x+c_z of all three triangles near the
identity. The middle plane transforms to

    n_l'=A_1^(-T)n_l,       h_l'=h_l+n_l'.c_1.

For each of the nine endpoint-vertex pairs (v0a,v2b), impose the smooth
inequality

    2h_l' - n_l'.(A_0 v0a+c_0+A_2 v2b+c_2)>=0.                    (2)

Together these are EXACTLY (1), not a linearized surrogate. At an active
middle facet, the active pairs are precisely vertices in
F(K0,n_l) x F(K2,n_l). All ties are thus included explicitly.

For infinitesimal A_z=I+B_z, the derivative of an active pair constraint is

    2 n_l.(B_1 m+c_1)
      -n_l.(B_0 r_0+c_0)-n_l.(B_2 r_2+c_2),                        (3)

where r_0=v0a, r_2=v2b and m=(r_0+r_2)/2 lies on F(K1,n_l).

## 2. Normalized stress and the contact measures

The middle remains deepest at any local minimum, since enlarging it is
always compatible and otherwise strictly decreases the endpoint maxima.
There cannot be two deepest endpoints, even for arbitrary convex fibers.
Let their unnormalized continuous depths be D0,D2 at centers y0,y2. At the
actual middle point (1,(y0+y2)/2), every middle continuous cap has volume at
least ((sqrt(D0)+sqrt(D2))/2)^2 by the pointwise Brunn--Minkowski cap argument.
Every ambient halfspace through this point also contains at least one of the
two endpoint deepest points, contributing at least min(D0,D2). Hence if both
endpoint depths equal D, the middle depth is at least2D>D. Only at most two
groups can carry stress.

Use the same middle critical circuit and canonical endpoint isolating
circuits as in candidate f3e1e26ab17d09a3, and the same
linear whole-fiber coverage constraints in the cap parameters.

The first-order separation remains normalized despite active compatibility.
Common inner parallel erosion preserves midpoint compatibility:

    ((K0 minus tB)+(K2 minus tB))/2+tB
       is contained in (K0+K2)/2 and hence in K1.

Here minus denotes inner parallel erosion. This gives nonnegative derivatives
of every active pair constraint. For triangles each erosion is an affine
homothety about its incenter. Add a sufficiently small positive multiple of
a middle-only outward parallel expansion. This increases every active pair
constraint to first order by2 times that multiple, while every active cap
generalized derivative remains strictly negative. Therefore all nonlinear
compatibility constraints can be strictified simultaneously with the cap
budgets; the remaining coverage constraints are linear. The usual finite
separation argument applies to their linearized cone, and a strict feasible
first-order direction integrates to an actual nearby feasible path because
(2) is smooth.

Let eta_l,ab>=0 be the pair-constraint multipliers. Group them as

    eta_l=sum_ab eta_l,ab,
    r_l0=(sum_ab eta_l,ab v0a)/eta_l,
    r_l2=(sum_ab eta_l,ab v2b)/eta_l,
    m_l=(r_l0+r_l2)/2,

when eta_l>0. Then r_le lies in the corresponding endpoint support face and
m_l lies on the middle facet. The grouped compatibility derivative is exactly
eta_l times (3). No claim that the endpoint contact is a unique vertex is
needed. If eta_l=0 its contact means may be chosen arbitrarily.

The normalized objective stress has the sign

    dM = sum_cap lambda_j (cap derivative)
             -sum_l eta_l (compatibility derivative_l)
             -sum_z coverage_multiplier_z dC_z.                  (4)

Joint homothety of the three bodies and the cap integer normals/thresholds
still gives

    sum_cap lambda_j=1/beta,                                     (5)

since every active compatibility and coverage constraint is homogeneous and
zero at the base point.

## 3. The exact change in the middle section equations

Put the middle circuit anchor at continuous0. Let C_j,S_j,X_j be its middle
cap area, section length and section first moment, with unit cap normals u_j.
The middle caps are proper cuts of that fiber, so these terms are ordinary
section derivatives. The canonical endpoint caps strictly exclude it.

Independent middle affine variations in (4) yield

    sum_middle lambda_j S_j u_j=2 sum_l eta_l n_l,                 (6)

and, for every matrix B,

    b tr(B)=sum_middle lambda_j[C_j tr(B)+u_j.B X_j]
                     -2 sum_l eta_l n_l.B m_l.                   (7)

Let T1=sum_l eta_l h_l, where h_l>0 because the anchor is interior to K1.
Since n_l.m_l=h_l and the middle cap planes pass through0, the trace gives

    sum_middle lambda_j C_j=b+T1.                                (8)

The remaining matrix equation is

    sum_middle lambda_j X_j u_j^T
       =-T1 I+2 sum_l eta_l m_l n_l^T.                            (9)

These are the exact contact-force replacements for zero continuous-normal
balance and common section centroids. In particular one cannot apply the
bisected-chord triangle lemma directly to (6)--(9).

## 4. The endpoint bound has an additional nonnegative budget

For an endpoint e which is deepest, write c_e for its triangle centroid and
A_e for its area. Dilation of this endpoint about c_e has objective derivative
2 A_e and derivative 2 gamma A_e on each of its canonical isolating caps.
Every middle-cap generalized shape derivative is nonnegative under this
expansion. The compatibility contribution in (4) is now positive and equals

    T_e=sum_l eta_l [h_Ke(n_l)-n_l.c_e]>=0.

It is strictly positive if any eta_l>0. Thus

    sum_(endpoint group) lambda_j
       <=1/gamma-T_e/(2 gamma A_e).                              (10)

So active contacts consume some endpoint multiplier budget. Whether that
budget controls the increase allowed in the middle group is unresolved.

The offsets must be tracked rather than identified without proof. Since
2h_l=h_K0(n_l)+h_K2(n_l) on active facets,

    2T1=T0+T2+sum_l eta_l n_l.(c_0+c_2),                           (11)

in coordinates where the middle circuit anchor is0. There is generally no
reason for the last centroid-displacement term to vanish.

## 5. A concrete fully active pattern that can be solved exactly

A useful special pattern is that all three triangles have the SAME three
facet normal directions and all three constraints (1) are equalities.
Triangles with a fixed three-direction normal fan differ by a translation
and a positive homothety. Their Minkowski average is again such a triangle,
with support offsets equal to the averages. Hence in this additional pattern

    K1=(K0+K2)/2

exactly, and the three ordinary centroids satisfy c_1=(c_0+c_2)/2.
This equality is NOT inferred merely from three tight supports for arbitrarily
rotated endpoint triangles.

More generally, whenever three positive d-dimensional convex fibers have
ordinary centroids satisfying c_1=(c_0+c_2)/2, the OC bound gamma_d/2 follows
directly. If any fiber has at least half the total volume, use its centroid
and its own continuous Grünbaum guarantee. Otherwise write their volumes as
a,b,c. A halfspace through the middle centroid also contains at least one
endpoint centroid, because the ambient middle point is their midpoint.
Its mass is therefore at least

    gamma_d [b+min(a,c)] >= gamma_d (a+b+c)/2,

where the last inequality is exactly max(a,c)<=b+min(a,c), true when no
endpoint is heavier than half the total. This handles every oblique closed
halfspace and uses one actual mixed-integer middle point.

Thus the common-normal fully tight pattern is settled. General active
patterns retain the explicit contact terms (6)--(11); rotated endpoint
triangles can give a strict hexagonal average inside K1 even when all three
middle supports are tight.

## 6. The active-boundary constraint qualification extends to polygons

For arbitrary positive polygon fibers, choose q0 in int(K0), q2 in int(K2)
and q1=(q0+q2)/2. The midpoint of two interior balls shows q1 is interior to
(K0+K2)/2 and therefore interior to K1. Simultaneously shrink each fiber
about qz by the same factor1-t. Since qz is affine in z, this is one ambient
affine fiber map. It preserves midpoint compatibility exactly, including all
active equalities. Every polygon facet moves strictly inward, so every
active cap-gradient choice has strictly negative pairing with this direction.

A middle-only outward homothety about q1 has, on each active support
constraint, derivative2 n_l.(m_l-q1)>0. Adding a sufficiently small positive
multiple makes all active compatibility derivatives strict while retaining
strict decrease of all active cap-gradient choices. Thus the normalized
contact dual (3)--(11) is valid for arbitrary polygons under independent
affine variables, with one contact group per active middle facet. The number
of possible active facets is then not bounded by3. This statement concerns
the dual only; the additional contact forces remain to be controlled.
